results.outcome: Dynamic lung stress (dynamic driving transpulmonary pressure, ΔPLdyn) during PEEP_EIT-ΔPL vs PEEP_TABLE — the first physiological outcome reported in the abstract results and the outcome on which the sample size was based (no outcome is explicitly named 'primary')
results.numerical_result: Mean difference in ΔPLdyn −1.7 [95% CI: −2.64 to −0.73] cmH2O; P < 0.001 (Fig. 1A, B; ESM Table E1)
results.result_location: Page 5 (p. 2129), section 'Physiologic effects of PEEP_EIT-ΔPL'; Figure 1A,B page 6 (p. 2130)

1.1.support: patients were ventilated with each PEEP for 20 min in a random computer-generated order (R software)

1.2.support: Randomization was performed centrally, and participating centres were notified of the result by telephone

1.3.support: Baseline characteristics are reported only for the whole cohort (Table 1); the report gives no data on patient characteristics stratified by order of PEEP strategy, so baseline differences at the start of the first period could not be examined.

S.1.support: The order of PEEP strategies was well balanced: 16 (53%) subjects were assigned to PEEP_EIT-ΔPL as the first study step

4.1.support: Airway and esophageal pressure (Paw and Pes) were continuously monitored by a dedicated system (PulmoVista 500, Dräger, Lübeck, Germany) and PL was calculated as the difference between Paw and Pes. Dynamic driving PL (ΔPLdyn) was calculated as the difference between the maximal inspiratory and end-expiratory PL.

4.2.support: Towards the end of each 20-min study step (PEEP_EIT-ΔPL and PEEP_TABLE), the following data were collected

4.3.support: as the main outcome involved analysis of airway pressure waveforms, blinding the assessors to study interventions was not feasible

4.4.support: ΔPLdyn was calculated as the difference between the maximal inspiratory and end-expiratory PL, an objective waveform-derived measure obtained identically in both steps, so knowledge of the assigned PEEP is unlikely to have systematically influenced its assessment.

4.5.support: Conditional on Y/PY/NI to 4.4; 4.4 was answered PN.

5.1.support: The report does not include the trial protocol or statistical analysis plan, so it could not be verified that the analysis of ΔPLdyn was pre-specified and finalized before unblinded outcome data were available.
5.1.location: Whole report; no protocol or SAP is printed

5.2.support: Dynamic lung stress was defined a priori as ΔPLdyn (calculated as maximal inspiratory minus end-expiratory PL), leaving essentially one eligible measurement for this outcome domain; no alternative definitions or time points are reported.

5.3.support: Analysis intentions are not available in sufficient detail: the report presents a paired analysis with an order-by-strategy interaction test, but without a protocol or SAP it cannot be determined whether other eligible analyses (e.g. with or without period effect) were considered and one selected on the basis of the results.

5.4.support: Data from both study steps contribute to the result; the report states 'The order in which the 2 PEEP strategies were provided did not affect the results', and no result was restricted to the first period on the basis of a carryover test.

D1.rationale: Random computer-generated sequence with central randomization and telephone notification (adequate generation and concealment); no baseline data by sequence were given (1.3 NI), which the algorithm does not elevate above low when generation and concealment are adequate.

DS.rationale: Sequence allocation was nearly equal (16/30 vs 14/30), and although there was no washout, the authors pre-justified the 20-min steps with references and empirically found no order effect (interaction P = 0.932 for ΔPLdyn), so period and carryover effects are unlikely to bias the result.

D2.rationale: Patients were sedated and unaware of allocation; clinicians necessarily knew the PEEP level, but no deviations from the intended interventions arose from the trial context, ventilation settings and sedation were held constant, and the paired analysis is appropriate for the effect of assignment.

D3.rationale: ΔPLdyn was available for all 30 randomized patients in both study steps; the only missing variable (ScvO2 in 4 patients) is not the outcome assessed.

D4.rationale: The outcome was measured with an identical, objective, waveform-based method in both steps; although assessors were unblinded, the measurement is quantitative and unlikely to be influenced by knowledge of the assigned PEEP.

D5.rationale: No protocol or statistical analysis plan was available, so it could not be confirmed that the analysis plan was pre-specified (5.1 NI) and whether multiple eligible analyses (e.g. with/without period effect) were considered and one selected (5.3 NI); the measurement itself appears uniquely defined, and both periods contribute to the result.

overall.rationale: All domains except selection of the reported result are at low risk of bias; D5 raises some concerns because pre-specification of the analysis could not be verified from the report, but these do not substantially lower confidence on their own.
